digest.component_or_area: op-cert service signing and key provisioning
propositions: Per-job boto3/SSM/region lookup in op-cert service couples app config to one secret store and creates concurrency/cleanup hazards; startup binding moves key acquisition to initialization before queue/worker/network/workspace creation.
Key source validation must reject missing, both-set, unreadable, non-regular, malformed, encrypted, or non-Ed25519 input; path sources require 0600-or-stricter file mode checks before service work.

Process-owned copy of signing material must be placed in 0700 directory with 0600 file permissions, remain stable for process lifetime, observe replacement only after restart, and cleanup must never alter the deployment source.

Both out-of-opcert_service/ signing producer chains (completion via sign_completion_verdict and plan-review via generation.sign_manifest) must thread immutable context-local signer/principal/push-policy bindings through jobs, eliminating os.environ patching.

Op-cert application runtime must not depend on SSM/boto3/region at runtime; the key must be materialized before service start via fetch-secrets.sh to a 0600 file bind-mounted read-only with REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH.

Concurrent and timed-out jobs must demonstrate context-local signer/principal/push-policy isolation with one immutable startup signer, no workspace push remote, and existing signature verification compatibility.
